In [[mathematics]], '''Peetre's inequality,''' named after [[Jaak Peetre]], says that for any [[real number]] <math>t</math> and any [[Vector space|vector]]s <math>x</math> and <math>y</math> in <math>\Reals^n,</math> the following [[Inequality (mathematics)|inequality]] holds:
<math display=block>\left(\frac{1+|x|^2}{1+|y|^2}\right)^t ~\leq~ 2^{|t|} (1+|x-y|^2)^{|t|}.</math>

The inequality was proved by J. Peetre in 1959 and has founds applications in [[functional analysis]] and [[Sobolev space]]s.
